_comment: Test Twin Propeller Aircraft (TTPA) requirements for IHW3, the SIZING LOOP. This file REPLACES Ttpa_requirements_IHW2.json for IHW3: read this one and only this one. It carries the aerodynamics, propulsion, constraints and missions blocks of IHW2 forward, and adds what a sizing loop needs that neither earlier homework had: a real geometry block (wing planform, tail volume coefficients, fuselage layout, nacelle), a weights block (Raymer Table 15.2 component build-up), Level-2 mission options, and a sizing block (guesses, tolerance, relaxation).
_what_changed_from_IHW2: Three things that were FIXED in IHW1/IHW2 are now OUTPUTS of the loop. (1) W_TO was 5354 lbf, the converged answer of the IHW1 mission analysis, typed into the IHW2 driver by hand. (2) S_ref and P_SL were computed ONCE from that W_TO and a chosen design point. (3) OEW came from the regression 0.911*W_TO^0.947, so it depended on nothing but weight. In IHW3 the geometry is rebuilt from S_ref on every pass, OEW is built up from that geometry and that engine, CD0 follows the wetted area, the cruise constraint and the mission fuel both follow CD0, and the takeoff weight closes on all of it.
_who_reads_what: geometry -> TtpaGeom. aerodynamics -> TtpaAero. propulsion -> TtpaProp. weights -> TtpaWeights. sizing -> run_ttpa_sizing_mainloop, which hands it to sizing_mainloop. constraints.conditions -> ConstraintSetImporter.read_conditions, then get_con. constraints.design_point -> run_ttpa_sizing_mainloop, for the first power guess only. missions -> MissionProfileReader.read_profile, then get_miss_seg, run_mission_L2 and mission_fuel.

geometry._comment: Imported external geometry from AmphibiousSeaplane_Concept1.vsp3. Coordinates are interpreted as feet.
geometry._what_is_an_input_here: Only SHAPE lives in this block - ratios, angles and the fixed cabin-driven fuselage. SIZE does not: S_ref is written by the sizing loop from W_TO and the wing loading, and every span, chord, area and wetted area is a Dependent property of TtpaGeom recomputed from S_ref on every read. No derived quantity is stored here or in the class.
geometry._src_AR: Derived from the supplied OpenVSP model. See geometry.openvsp for source values, coordinates, units and limitations.
geometry._src_taper_ratio: Derived from the supplied OpenVSP model. See geometry.openvsp for source values, coordinates, units and limitations.
geometry._src_sweep_quarter_chord_deg: Derived from the supplied OpenVSP model. See geometry.openvsp for source values, coordinates, units and limitations.
geometry._src_thickness_ratio: Derived from the supplied OpenVSP model. See geometry.openvsp for source values, coordinates, units and limitations.
geometry._src_twist_incidence_dihedral: Derived from the supplied OpenVSP model. See geometry.openvsp for source values, coordinates, units and limitations.

horizontal_tail._src: OpenVSP fixed surface. Arm is distance between wing and tail quarter-MAC stations; it is not a CG-referenced stability validation.

vertical_tail._src: OpenVSP fixed surface. Arm is distance between wing and tail quarter-MAC stations; it is not a CG-referenced stability validation.

fuselage._comment: OpenVSP external fuselage sections; 0-11.25 ft nose, 11.25-24.3 ft full-width region, 24.3-45 ft aft body. Internal usable cabin requires layout.
fuselage._src_width_height: OpenVSP external fuselage sections; 0-11.25 ft nose, 11.25-24.3 ft full-width region, 24.3-45 ft aft body. Internal usable cabin requires layout.
fuselage._src_lengths: OpenVSP external fuselage sections; 0-11.25 ft nose, 11.25-24.3 ft full-width region, 24.3-45 ft aft body. Internal usable cabin requires layout.
fuselage._src_tailcone_end: OpenVSP external fuselage sections; 0-11.25 ft nose, 11.25-24.3 ft full-width region, 24.3-45 ft aft body. Internal usable cabin requires layout.

nacelle._comment: OpenVSP external pod dimensions and evaluated wetted area. Check engine fit separately.
nacelle._src_diameter_ft: OpenVSP external pod dimensions and evaluated wetted area. Check engine fit separately.
nacelle._src_length_over_engine_length: OpenVSP external pod dimensions and evaluated wetted area. Check engine fit separately.

landing_gear._comment: Tricycle gear. These two ratios convert the converged takeoff weight into the static loads the struts and tyres are sized to. They are used AFTER the loop converges, not inside it - the gear WEIGHT inside the loop is the Raymer Table 15.2 fraction of W_TO.
landing_gear._src: Raymer Ch. 11: the static load on the main gear is W * l_n/l_d and on the nose gear is W * l_m/l_d, where l_d is the nose-to-main wheelbase, l_n the aft-cg-to-nose-gear distance and l_m the forward-cg-to-main-gear distance. Until a weight-and-balance study fixes the cg envelope, 0.90 and 0.15 are the standard placeholders.

concept1._note: Screening geometry assumptions from the Concept 1 context. High-wing/T-tail placement and water hydrodynamics are not resolved by these parameters.

openvsp.units_basis: Assumed feet from 45-unit fuselage, 60-unit wing and 8-unit propeller. OpenVSP shape coordinates have no authoritative physical unit.
openvsp.reference_area_basis: OpenVSP TotalArea, projected span used for AR; excludes rotating propeller surfaces from airframe wetted area.
limitations: CompGeom reports two open meshes merged; surface areas use the supplied default tessellation.
External hull volume is not watertight underfloor buoyancy or floodable compartment volume.
No static waterline, internal cabin boundaries, landing gear or engine integration envelope are established by these surfaces.
openvsp.revision_note: Enlarged wing and tails, raised horizontal tail with taller fin, and moved floats/struts outboard with wing.

aerodynamics._comment: Carried over from IHW2, with ONE addition and ONE change of role. The addition is Cfe. The change is CD0_clean: it is no longer the model, it is the CROSS-CHECK. In IHW2 the clean CD0 was a fixed 0.028 read straight out of this file. In IHW3 the airplane has real geometry, so TtpaAero computes the clean CD0 from the wetted area instead, and CD0_clean stays here as the IHW2 value to compare against. Everything else in this block - the three CLmax values, the stall margin, the flap, gear and propeller increments - is unchanged and is still read exactly the same way.
aerodynamics._how_the_configuration_polar_is_built: CD0_config = CD0_clean + the flap increment + the gear increment (+ the stopped-propeller increment in the engine-out climb). e_config = e_clean + the flap increment, where e_clean is still computed from the aspect ratio inside TtpaAero. K1_config = 1/(pi*AR*e_config). CLmax_config is read directly from the three CLmax keys below.
aerodynamics._src_CD0_clean: Clean (cruise) zero-lift drag coefficient. Same value that was hardcoded in the IHW1 TtpaAero; it now comes from this file so that there is exactly one place to change it.
aerodynamics._role_of_CD0_clean_in_IHW3: REFERENCE VALUE, not a model input. TtpaAero.CD0 is a Dependent property computed from the geometry with Raymer Eq. 12.23. The run script prints both; they agree to about one percent, and that agreement is the check that the geometry and the wetted-area build-up are right.
aerodynamics._src_Cfe: NEW IN IHW3. Raymer Table 12.3, equivalent skin-friction coefficient for a light TWIN-engine airplane (the single-engine row is 0.0055). Used with Raymer Eq. 12.23, CD0 = Cfe * S_wet / S_ref, to get the clean zero-lift drag of the airplane the loop has just laid out. This is the single equation that couples GEOMETRY to DRAG, and therefore to mission fuel and to takeoff weight.
aerodynamics._src_CLmax: Roskam Part I, Table 3.1 (twin-engine propeller-driven, FAR 23): clean 1.2-1.8, takeoff 1.4-2.0, landing 1.6-2.6. Mid-range values assumed for the TTPA. Pull the one that matches the configuration of the condition you are evaluating: clean for the engine-out climb, takeoff for the takeoff ground roll and the all-engines climb, landing for the landing ground roll and the balked landing.
aerodynamics._src_CL_stall_margin: Roskam Part I, Sec. 3.3. The steepest climb is flown near CLmax, which is unsafe because the airplane is then close to the stall, so the climb lift coefficient is taken 0.2 below the CLmax of that configuration. Apply it inside get_config_polar so that no constraint function can forget it.
aerodynamics._src_delta_CD0: Roskam Part I, Table 3.6, zero-lift drag increments: takeoff flaps 0.010-0.020, landing flaps 0.055-0.075, landing gear extended 0.015-0.025. Mid-range values assumed. The gear increment adds on top of the flap increment when the gear is down.
aerodynamics._src_delta_e: Roskam Part I, Table 3.6, Oswald-efficiency increments: about -0.05 with takeoff flaps and about -0.10 with landing flaps. Extending the gear does not change e.
aerodynamics._src_delta_CD0_propeller_stopped: Roskam Part I, Sec. 3.3: drag increment of the stopped propeller of the failed engine. Add it only when the condition sets propeller_stopped, which is the one-engine-inoperative climb.
aerodynamics._src_CLmax_landing: Retained high-lift target, requires validation for the revised wing.

propulsion._comment: Carried over from IHW2 with the engine-size regression added. IHW2 needed to know how much power the engine MAKES; the sizing loop also needs to know how much it WEIGHS and how long it is, because the first feeds the empty weight and the second feeds the nacelle wetted area, and both follow from P_SL - one of the two states the loop iterates on.
propulsion._src_n_engines: NEW. Twin-engine airplane. In the one-engine-inoperative climb only 1 of the 2 engines is running, so the available power is divided by this number.
propulsion._src_BSFC: Carried over from IHW1. Preliminary brake-specific fuel consumption of the piston engine, used by the cruise and loiter mission segments.
propulsion._src_eta_p_mission: Carried over from IHW1. Propeller efficiencies of the cruise and loiter mission segments.
propulsion._src_eta_p_climb: NEW. Propeller efficiency in a climb. The climb-gradient constraint needs it, and the mission analysis never did, because IHW1 modelled climb with a fixed weight fraction.
propulsion._src_P_TO_over_P_max_continuous: NEW. Roskam Part I, Sec. 3.3: for a typical piston engine the takeoff power is about 1.1 times the maximum continuous power. The all-engines climb must be flown at maximum continuous power, so the power available there is the takeoff power divided by this number.
propulsion._src_engine_regression: NEW IN IHW3. Raymer Table 10.4, British block, horizontally-opposed piston column: W_engine = 5.47 * bhp^0.780 [lb] and L_engine = 0.32 * bhp^0.424 [ft], both PER ENGINE, with bhp the rated power of ONE engine. Horizontally-opposed is the right column: Raymer Sec. 10.5 notes that opposed engines now dominate general aviation. Divide P_SL by n_engines before using these.
propulsion._src_bhp_range_of_validity: Raymer Table 10.4 prints 60-500 bhp as the applicable range of the opposed-engine regression. TtpaProp warns, and does not error, when the loop asks for a per-engine power outside it: an intermediate iterate can leave the band and come back.
propulsion._src_turboprop_dry_weight_lbf: Optional fixed dry weight per engine for a documented engine. Null uses the power-scaled estimate.
propulsion._concept1_power_note: P_SL is the reference power. Each power source is provisionally rated to P_SL (ratios 1.0), so either source can independently provide that reference power. They are not summed in the current operating schedule.
propulsion._concept1_data_note: BSFC, efficiencies, battery specific energy, motor specific power, turboprop specific weight, and length are preliminary assumptions from the project context, not supplier specifications.
propulsion._src_selected_engine: Prior selected twin PT6A-34 sensitivity, constant BSFC and flat altitude power remain screening assumptions. Geometry import does not establish installed engine performance.

weights._comment: NEW IN IHW3. In IHW1 and IHW2 the empty weight was one line inside TtpaWeights, OEW = 0.911 * W_TO^0.947, and the payload was a literal 1200. That regression knows only the takeoff weight: build a bigger wing or hang a bigger engine on the same airplane and it returns the same answer. A sizing loop needs an empty weight that RESPONDS to the airplane it has just laid out, so IHW3 replaces it with the Raymer Table 15.2 component build-up. The old regression is kept below as a cross-check and is reported next to the build-up.
weights._the_buildup: OEW = wing + horizontal tail + vertical tail + fuselage + landing gear + installed engines + all-else-empty. The first four are an areal density times an area; the last three are fractions. Raymer Table 15.2, General Aviation column throughout.
weights._src_W_payload: Tidal Flight Seaplane RFP 2026: 9 passengers and 2 pilots at 180 lb each plus 9 passenger bags at 50 lb each = 2,430 lb.
weights._src_unit_weights: Raymer Table 15.2, General Aviation column. The wing and the two tails multiply EXPOSED PLANFORM area; the fuselage multiplies WETTED area. Mixing those two multipliers up is the classic error with this table - the fuselage row is the only wetted one.
weights._src_landing_gear_fraction: Raymer Table 15.2, General Aviation, times TOGW. The table footnote splits it 15 percent nose and 85 percent main, and says to subtract 0.014*W_0 for fixed gear. The TTPA retracts, so the full 0.057 applies.
weights._src_installed_engine_factor: Raymer Table 15.2, General Aviation, times the BARE ENGINE WEIGHT of all engines. Note that the GA column is 1.4, not the 1.3 of the fighter and transport columns. It covers the mount, the cowl, the exhaust, the starter and the rest of the installation. The bare engine weight comes from the Table 10.4 regression in the propulsion block.
weights._src_all_else_empty_fraction: Raymer Table 15.2, General Aviation, times TOGW. Covers flight controls, instruments, hydraulics, electrics, avionics, air conditioning and furnishings in one term. The GA column is 0.1; the fighter and transport columns are 0.17.
weights._src_statistical_OEW: The IHW1 empty-weight regression, OEW = 0.911 * W_TO^0.947, from the Nicolai light-propeller-airplane trend. KEPT AS A CROSS-CHECK ONLY. TtpaWeights.OEW now returns the component build-up; TtpaWeights.OEW_statistical returns this, and the run script prints both. They should agree within a few percent. If they do not, the geometry is wrong.
weights._src_fuel_density_lb_per_ft3: BACK-DERIVED, NOT AN INDEPENDENT MEASUREMENT. The course wing-layout notebook states that a 37 ft^3 wing holds 1770 lb of 100LL 'at low temperature', and 1770/37 = 47.8 lb/ft^3. That value is adopted here so the fuel-volume check reproduces the course number. For reference, 100LL at 15 degC is about 6.0 lb/US gal = 44.9 lb/ft^3, which would give 1562 lb of capacity instead of 1663 lb - still far above the roughly 1019 lb the mission needs, so the conclusion of the check does not depend on which figure is used. Used only AFTER the loop converges.

concept1._note: Concept 1 screening weight factors; battery weight remains in W_energy, outside OEW.

_src_design_range_nmi: Converted from the 1,000 statute-mile minimum-range requirement using 1 nmi = 1.15077945 statute mi; rounded to 0.001 nmi.

sizing._comment: Everything the main sizing loop needs that is not a property of the airplane: where to start, when to stop, and how hard to damp each step. Read by run_ttpa_sizing_mainloop and passed to sizing_mainloop. No discipline class reads this block.
sizing._the_framework: Three states are iterated to a consistent set: the takeoff weight W_0, the sea-level shaft power P_0, and the wing area S_ref. AR and taper are held constant. Each pass: (1) constraint analysis on the current airplane gives the least-engine corner (W/S, W/P); (2) S_ref = W_0/(W/S) and P_0 = W_0/(W/P); (3) the mission gives the fuel; (4) the build-up gives OEW; (5) W_0_new = W_payload/(1 - W_f/W_0 - OEW/W_0); (6) stop when W_0 and P_0 both stop moving, otherwise relax all three states and go again. S_ref is an OUTPUT.
sizing._src_W_TO_guess_lbf: The same starting guess IHW1 used. The first power guess is W_TO_guess/(W/P) at constraints.design_point. The loop reaches the same answer from anywhere between 2500 and 10000 lbf, so this is a convenience, not an input to the answer. Change it and check that nothing moves: that is the test that the fixed point is real.
sizing._src_S_ref_guess_ft2: Starting guess for the wing area only. The first pass replaces it with W_0/(W/S). Any value from 90 to 200 ft^2 reaches the same converged wing.
sizing._src_tol_max_iter: Relative tolerance on BOTH states. The loop stops only when |W_new - W_0|/W_new and |P_new - P_0|/P_new are both below tol_rel. 1e-6 is the metabook TOGW test. The loop takes about 35 passes, so 200 is a generous ceiling.
sizing._src_relaxation: Under-relaxation factor in (0,1] applied to all three states: x <- x + w*(x_new - x). Numerical damping, not physics: at the converged point x_new = x, so w cannot change the answer, only the path to it. It is NOT optional. A full step (w = 1) overshoots by about 2.5 times per pass and lands where the empty weight and the fuel consume the whole takeoff weight. Measured on this airplane, all reaching the same answer to 0.003 lbf: w = 0.70 and above fail, 0.60 takes 49 passes, 0.50 takes 95, 0.45 takes 34, 0.30 takes 49, 0.15 takes 103.

constraints._comment: NEW IN IHW2. The requirements the matching diagram is built from. Read the conditions with ConstraintSetImporter.read_conditions(json_path), which returns a 1x6 struct array in the order below; get_con then pulls one of them out. Each condition holds REQUIREMENT data only: where the airplane is, in what configuration, at what weight and power, and what it must achieve there. No CLmax, no CD0, no propeller efficiency and no power lapse appears here - all of those come from your TtpaAero and TtpaProp objects at run time.
constraints._note_missing_keys: The six conditions do not all carry the same keys: a field-length condition has distance_ft, a climb condition has G, the cruise condition has ktas and power_index. Where a key is absent the importer leaves an empty value ([]), so read the optional keys through a helper that returns a default. The defaults are beta = 1.0, power_setting = 1.0, config = clean, and false for the three logical flags.
constraints._note_beta: beta = W_condition / W_TO, the weight at which the condition must be met, referred to takeoff weight. It is a SPECIFIED REQUIREMENT INPUT, not an output of your mission analysis. beta = 0.975 is the weight after startup, taxi, takeoff and the initial climb: Roskam Part I Table 2.2 gives 0.984 for startup/taxi/takeoff and 0.990 for climb, and 0.984 x 0.990 = 0.974, which is the same pair of fractions your IHW1 run_mission applies. It represents an airplane that loses an engine or returns to the field soon after takeoff.
constraints._note_power_setting: power_setting is the throttle fraction of the rated power at that condition (1.0 = full power). The altitude power lapse, the maximum-continuous derate and the one-engine-inoperative split are NOT stored here: your TtpaProp applies them from n_engines, P_TO_over_P_max_continuous and the flags on the condition.
constraints._note_config: config names the flap and landing-gear position. The five names your get_config_polar must accept are clean, takeoff_flaps_gear_up, takeoff_flaps_gear_down, landing_flaps_gear_up and landing_flaps_gear_down. They are the names the framework uses in AerodynamicsBase.get_config_polar.
constraints._src_wing_loading_range_psf: Wing-loading sweep of the matching diagram, lbf/ft^2, and the number of points on it. Read by the driver script, not by any constraint function: every constraint function receives the sweep as its first argument.

conditions.name: Takeoff
conditions._src: Takeoff ground roll of 1,500 ft at sea level, and the climb to 50 ft above the takeoff surface of 14 CFR 23.2115. Sized with the FAR 23 takeoff parameter, Roskam Part I Sec. 3.1: S_TGR = 4.9 TOP23 + 0.009 TOP23^2, with TOP23 = (W/S)(W/P) / (sigma CLmax_TO). beta = 1.0 because takeoff happens at takeoff weight by definition.
conditions._src_distance_ft: Concept 1 maximum runway takeoff distance over a 50 ft obstacle.

conditions.name: Landing
conditions._src: Landing ground roll of 1,500 ft at sea level after a 50-ft obstacle, 14 CFR 23.2130. Sized with Roskam Part I Sec. 3.2: S_LGR = 0.265 Vs_L^2, with S_LGR in ft and Vs_L in kt. This condition limits the wing loading only; it does not constrain the power loading.
conditions._src_distance_ft: Inherited professor baseline landing-field distance (1,500 ft), not a confirmed Concept 1 requirement.

conditions.name: Climb AEO
conditions._src: 14 CFR 23.2120 (Part 23 Level 2, low speed), all engines operating: minimum climb gradient of 8.3 % with the landing gear retracted, the flaps in the takeoff position and both engines at maximum continuous power. max_continuous = true is what makes your TtpaProp divide the available power by P_TO_over_P_max_continuous.

conditions.name: Climb OEI
conditions._src: 14 CFR 23.2120 (Part 23 Level 2, low speed), one engine inoperative: minimum climb gradient of 1.5 % at 5,000 ft with the landing gear and the flaps retracted and the remaining engine at takeoff power. oei = true divides the available power by n_engines; propeller_stopped = true adds the stopped-propeller drag increment of the failed engine.

conditions.name: Climb BL
conditions._src: 14 CFR 23.2120 (Part 23 Level 2, low speed), balked landing: minimum climb gradient of 3.0 % with the landing gear extended, the flaps in the landing position and both engines at takeoff power.

conditions.name: Cruise Speed
conditions._src: Minimum cruise speed of 200 KTAS at 8,000 ft. Sized with the power index of Roskam Part I Sec. 3.6, Ip = [ (W/S) / (sigma (W/P)) ]^(1/3), read from Fig. 3.28 at 200 kt as Ip = 1.4. The cruise power of a propeller-driven airplane is set to 80 % of the rated power, which is power_setting. No beta is given because the cruise weight cancels: it divides the wing loading and the power loading by the same factor. ktas is the requirement this condition came from and is carried for reporting; the analysis itself uses power_index.
conditions._src_method: IHW3 uses 'drag_based'. 'power_index' is the Roskam Part I Sec. 3.6 correlation of IHW2, W/P <= (W/S)*kP/(sigma*Ip^3); it does NOT read the drag polar, so it cannot notice that the wing changed. 'drag_based' is the actual power balance at the required speed: q = 0.5*rho*V^2, C_L = beta*(W/S)/q, C_D = CD0 + K1*C_L^2, and W/P <= 550*eta_p*kP/(beta*V*(C_D/C_L)). Because it reads CD0, and CD0 reads S_wet/S_ref, this is the constraint that couples the matching diagram to the geometry. Both methods stay in constraint_cruise_speed: set this key to 'power_index' to reproduce IHW2.
conditions._src_altitude_ktas: Concept 1 minimum cruise requirement; density altitude is represented using 10,000 ft standard-atmosphere state for this preliminary model.
conditions._src_power_setting: Inherited 0.80 cruise power setting from the professor baseline; not specified as a Concept 1 requirement. Review with the example mission.
conditions._src_beta: Provisional beta = 1.0 (takeoff weight at cruise), conservative until the mission fuel fraction establishes cruise weight.

constraints._workflow_note: Plot settings mirror Concept 3 structure. Active RFP conditions are constructed in concept1_rfp_constraints.m, retaining the Concept 1 hybrid equations. design_point is the Caravan comparison reference, not the selected Concept 1 point.

missions._comment: Carried over from IHW1 unchanged, so that your mission analysis runs against this file with no edit. Read with MissionProfileReader.read_profile(json_path, 'std_mission'), then one segment at a time with get_miss_seg. The constraint analysis needs the takeoff gross weight your mission analysis converges to.

std_mission._description: Provisional direct water-to-water mission from the Baltimore area to the New Orleans area, with the 45-minute IFR reserve loiter before destination landing.
std_mission._cite_reserve_fuel_fraction: 6% reserve/trapped-fuel allowance applied on top of the complete mission.
std_mission._src_cruise: Uses the Concept 1 provisional direct-flight mission: 1,000 statute-mile minimum design range, 180 KTAS, 10,000 ft. The example BWI-to-New Orleans airport-reference distance is about 857 nmi.
std_mission._src_loiter: 45-minute IFR reserve is a Concept 1 requirement. 4,000 ft loiter altitude and 120 KTAS are inherited professor-baseline assumptions pending the example mission.
std_mission._src_method: 'L1' is the IHW1 mission: Roskam Table 2.2 fixed fractions everywhere, cruise and loiter by Breguet at L/D_max and 0.866*L/D_max. 'L2' is the IMPROVED FUEL FRACTIONS of the sizing-refinement lecture: the lift coefficient is computed from the ACTUAL wing loading at each condition, so the fuel finally responds to the wing. The lecture draws this as the W_0/S_ref arrow into the Fuel fraction box, and it is the largest single error in the L1 mission - see _why_L2_matters.
std_mission._why_L2_matters: L2 computes cruise and loiter lift coefficients from the actual wing loading at each condition, so fuel burn responds to the selected wing and the mission flight conditions. The inherited sizing example narrative for 200 KTAS at 8,000 ft does not apply to this mission.
std_mission._src_cruise_segments: Twelve cruise subsegments are retained from the starter profile for numerical stability; verify convergence for this mission and wing loading when running the sizing code.
std_mission._src_climb_segments: Four climb subsegments are retained from the starter profile; the mission climbs to 10,000 ft.
std_mission._src_ground_segment_method: Inherited ground-segment method setting. The current example mission uses explicit water_takeoff and water_landing electric segments; water hydrodynamic resistance is not modeled.
std_mission._src_credit_climb_distance: The lecture allows the ground distance covered in the climb to be credited against the cruise range. Left OFF by default so the 1200 nmi cruise requirement means the same thing it did in IHW1 and IHW2. Turning it on shortens the cruise by roughly 8 nmi, which is inside the noise.
std_mission._src_reserve_fuel_fraction: No extra percentage reserve is applied in this starter profile; the 45-minute IFR reserve is represented by the explicit loiter segment. Do not apply the professor baseline 6% on top unless a separate requirement is established.
std_mission._mission_status: Provisional BWI-area to New Orleans-area direct mission. Uses 10,000 ft cruise (below the 15,000 ft unpressurized ceiling), 180 KTAS, 1,000 statute-mile design range, and a 45-minute IFR reserve loiter. Water takeoff and landing use the Cessna 208 screening schedule. Actual water-site locations remain to be confirmed.
std_mission._src_electric_segments: The mission treats water takeoff and water landing as electric-only. Positive durations are required by the mission code; power_fraction can be provided or left to its default full-rated electric shaft power.
std_mission._src_cruise_distance: Uses the 1,000 statute-mile design-range requirement (868.976 nmi), which is slightly longer than the BWI-to-New Orleans Lakefront airport-reference great-circle distance.

_model_status: Revised OpenVSP concept. Run run_concept1_openvsp for evaluated geometry and current pass/fail.
_concept1_assumptions_note: Values explicitly identified as inherited or provisional are assumptions, not new aircraft requirements.

aircraft_requirements._src_mtow_ceiling: Project operating objective. Use a certificated MTOW strictly below 12,500 lb. See 14 CFR 1.1 and 49 CFR 1544.101 and 1550.7.
aircraft_requirements.example_mission: Direct water-to-water Baltimore to New Orleans; no intermediate stop.

example_route.origin_reference: Baltimore/Washington International Airport (BWI) reference point; water takeoff site not specified.
example_route.destination_reference: New Orleans Lakefront Airport (NEW) reference point; water landing site not specified.
example_route.route_note: Airport reference points are geographic proxies only. Sizing cruise distance retains the 1,000 statute-mile minimum-range requirement, slightly longer than this direct route.
example_route.altitude_note: Uses the existing 10,000 ft cruise-density-altitude design point, below the 15,000 ft unpressurized operating ceiling.

analysis_design.note: Revised OpenVSP geometry with enlarged wing/tails; retains selected turbine, motor and pack targets. No drag reduction credited.
